skill.name: zarr-python
skill.description: Guide for building Zarr Python workflows with chunked arrays, compression, cloud storage, and NumPy, Dask, and Xarray integrations.
skill.summary: Create efficient Zarr Python storage workflows for large scientific arrays.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The static findings were documentation false positives involving markdown backticks, a Zarr group keys example, reference URLs, and performance wording. No prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or executable malware behavior was found. One low-severity semantic concern remains because the skill promotes the author hosted K-Dense Web service in runtime instructions.

remediation.issue: Proactive external service promotion in runtime instructions
remediation.suggestion: Remove the K-Dense Web suggestion from SKILL.md, or disclose it in marketplace metadata instead of runtime guidance.

static_findings.snippet: "Avoid loading entire large arrays into memory - process in chunks",
"Avoid frequent writes to the same cloud storage location without synchronization"
- Use consolidated metadata to reduce latency: `zarr.consolidate_metadata(store)`
- Speeds up `tree()` operations and group traversal
- **Balance**: Larger chunks = fewer metadata operations; smaller chunks = better parallel access

content.value_statement: Large scientific arrays are hard to store, compress, and process efficiently. This skill guides Zarr Python workflows for chunked storage, cloud backends, and parallel analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to create, open, resize, append, and index Zarr arrays.
Guides chunk size, chunk shape, sharding, and compression choices.
Shows local, memory, ZIP, S3, and Google Cloud Storage store patterns.
Covers groups, attributes, consolidated metadata, and hierarchical stores.
Describes NumPy, Dask, and Xarray workflows for larger-than-memory data.
Provides troubleshooting advice for latency, memory use, and concurrent writes.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not run Zarr operations for the user.
Cloud examples require user-managed credentials and storage permissions.
Examples may need updates for project-specific Zarr versions and dependencies.
It does not validate data schemas, access policies, or production security settings.

use_cases.title: Design a climate data store
use_cases.description: Plan chunks, groups, compression, and metadata for gridded weather or climate arrays.

use_cases.title: Move arrays to object storage
use_cases.description: Choose S3 or Google Cloud Storage patterns with consolidated metadata and cloud-sized chunks.

use_cases.title: Optimize parallel analysis
use_cases.description: Use Dask and Xarray with Zarr stores for lazy computation on large datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic Zarr array
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a local array store.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a local Zarr array for my dataset. Include shape, dtype, chunks, and a simple read example.

prompt_templates.title: Choose chunking and compression
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate performance planning for known access patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend chunk shape, chunk size, and compression for this array shape and access pattern: [describe dataset].

prompt_templates.title: Plan cloud storage layout
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced object storage design for shared datasets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Zarr layout for S3 or Google Cloud Storage. Include metadata consolidation, sharding, and write safety concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a slow Zarr pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Zarr workflow and identify likely causes of slow reads, high memory use, or concurrent write conflicts.

output_examples.input: I need to store a 3D time series that grows every day.
output_examples.output: A recommended layout with time-first chunks, append guidance, compression options, and notes about metadata updates.

output_examples.input: My S3 Zarr reads are slow when opening many arrays.
output_examples.output: A diagnosis focused on metadata round trips, chunk size, consolidated metadata, and sharding tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: I want to analyze a Zarr store with Xarray and Dask.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline for lazy opening, labeled selection, parallel computation, and controlled result writing.

best_practices: Choose chunks that match the most common read and write patterns.
Use consolidated metadata for cloud stores with many arrays or groups.
Use synchronizers or separate chunk ownership for concurrent writes.
anti_patterns: Do not load complete large arrays into memory when chunked processing works.
Do not use very small chunks that create excessive object and metadata overhead.
Do not update consolidated metadata from multiple writers without a clear coordination plan.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps design and troubleshoot Zarr Python workflows for large chunked array datasets.

faq.question: Does it run commands or install packages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The user controls any installation or execution.

faq.question: Can it help with S3 and Google Cloud Storage?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common store patterns, metadata consolidation, and chunk sizing for object storage.

faq.question: Is it useful with Dask and Xarray?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers lazy array access, parallel computation, labeled datasets, and Zarr-backed output.

faq.question: Can it choose the best chunk size for every dataset?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend options, but real workloads should be benchmarked with representative access patterns.

faq.question: Does it manage cloud credentials?
faq.answer: No. Users must configure credentials, permissions, and access policies outside the skill.
